1.1.text:
Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency. 5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection. 6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb. 11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 13. Child Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 36

1. Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
2. In providing assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

Article 34

1. The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Paragraph 1

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Women

Article 57

1. Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
2. Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 37

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government provides legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 39

1. Social reintegration as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to enable women and children as victims to resume their social life and have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 32

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil problems to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. In implementing services as referred to in paragraph (2), UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or existing social community organizations.

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:

d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.

a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Paragraph 1

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Women

Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 37

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government provides legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 39

1. Social reintegration as referred to in Article 38 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues with their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
2. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to enable women and children as victims to resume their social life and have a decent life.
3. Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Article 34

1. The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Paragraph 1

Rights of Women

Article 32

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil problems to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. In implementing services as referred to in paragraph (2), UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or existing social community organizations.

Article 36

1. Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
2. In providing assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER IV

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence is provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 34

1. The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 37

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government provides legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 48

Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 13. Child Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 27

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, which is carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.
3. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process of services needed by women and children who experience problems.
4. Every element within the UPTD PPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and openness, both within the UPTD PPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatuses, related agencies, and community elements.

Article 37

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
4. The Regional Government provides legal aid to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence is provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 34

1. The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter b may be provided by the Regional Government for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
2. The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 36

1. Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
2. In providing assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

Sufficiently clear

a. counseling;

Article 10

Article 34

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 32

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter c is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil problems to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
3. In implementing services as referred to in paragraph (2), UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or existing social community organizations.

Article 27

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, which is carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.
3. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process of services needed by women and children who experience problems.
4. Every element within the UPTD PPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and openness, both within the UPTD PPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatuses, related agencies, and community elements.

Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence is provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 37

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
3. Types of legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.

Article 36

1. Assistance services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
2. In providing assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
2. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
3. In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence is provided with formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the education unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 40

Repatriation and social reintegration of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues as referred to in Article 38 and Article 39 shall be implemented by UPTD PPA in accordance with laws and regulations.

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency. 5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection. 6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb. 11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 13. Child Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

Article 27

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, which is carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.
2. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for carrying out the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children who experience problems.
3. In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process of services needed by women and children who experience problems.
4. Every element within the UPTD PPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and openness, both within the UPTD PPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatuses, related agencies, and community elements.

Paragraph 2

Obligations Regarding the Protection of Children

Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 71

In carrying out its duties, the CFC Task Force as referred to in Article 70 paragraph (1) may coordinate and cooperate with the UPTD PPA and/or other institutions that provide protection services for women and children.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints in the following ways:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 67

1. In organizing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate, the Regional Government facilitates the establishment of a Children's Forum.
2. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents Children in the Region.
3. The representation as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of the geographical domicile of Children, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.
4. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) may be established at the Regional, Sub-district and Nagari levels.
5. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regional Government is obliged to consider and accommodate the opinions of Children submitted through the Children's Forum.
6. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 56

1. Every organizer of an education unit must provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

Article 10

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency. 5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection. 6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb. 11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 13. Child Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

Article 9

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 27

1. The implementation of UPTD PPA services is integrative, which is carried out under one roof or networked to provide optimal services to women and children who experience problems.

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and

Article 72

d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.

a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.

Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency. 5. Social Service, Women Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women and Child Protection. 6. Women Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including children still in the womb. 11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 12. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 13. Child Forum is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. 25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 29.

Article 37

Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter e constitute actions by law enforcement officers to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 72

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. the formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in organizing women's empowerment and child protection;
b. technical guidance and training, comprising:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement officers on the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in organizing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the establishment of nagari that care for women and children;
e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) The supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) comprises:
a. monitoring carried out in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months; and
b. evaluation of the organization of women's empowerment and child protection periodically once (1) in 3 (three) months carried out by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
5. Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent's Regulation.

Article 9

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;

c. supervise the law enforcement process in cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

3. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on statutory regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 30

1. Reports of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures for handling complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.
